comparison.item: Option A — Medi-Cal (MAGI New Adult Group)
comparison.value: Best when your MAGI is at or below 138% FPL ($22,025 for one person, 2026)
comparison.detail: Free or low cost. Dental and vision included. Year-round enrollment. Subject to the work rule and six-month renewals from 2027 if you are 19–64 and not exempt.

comparison.item: Option B — Medi-Cal, Aged & Disabled FPL program
comparison.value: Best if you have a qualifying disability and countable assets under the limit
comparison.detail: 138% FPL income limit, non-MAGI rules, assets counted. Not subject to the work rule or the six-month renewal cycle.

comparison.item: Option C — Covered California with federal credit and California Premium Subsidy
comparison.value: Best when your MAGI is above 138% FPL and at or below 400% FPL
comparison.detail: Premium help only. Open enrollment November 1, 2026 – January 31, 2027. California state help up to 200% FPL in 2027.

comparison.value: Best when you are above 400% FPL, or you lost Medi-Cal for work-rule non-compliance
comparison.detail: You pay the full premium. You can still buy coverage at any time if you have a qualifying life event.

option-a.value: California's Medicaid program, for adults 19–64 with household income up to 138% FPL
option-a.detail: "The MAGI New Adult Group … extends Medicaid eligibility to all adults aged 19 to 64, including those without dependent children and parents with income over 109% but at or below 138% of the federal poverty level." No asset test for this group.

option-a.item: Why it is the leading option for a zero-earned-income household
option-a.value: Your income is not $0 — it is your rental, interest and trading income, and that is what Medi-Cal measures
option-a.detail: There is no separate "no income" Medi-Cal program and no earned-income requirement. If your MAGI lands at or under 138% FPL, you qualify regardless of where the money comes from.

option-a.value: Free or low cost for most people
option-a.detail: Health, dental and vision. Separate premium rules start July 1, 2027 for some people with certain immigration statuses.

option-a.value: From January 1, 2027: 80 hours or $580 per month, and renewals twice a year
option-a.detail: This is the rule that changes everything for you. Use the $580 income test (rental, interest, and trading income count) or the 80-hour route, or claim an exemption.

option-a.value: Any time of year, one application for Medi-Cal and Covered California
option-a.detail: Online via BenefitsCal or Covered California, by mail, by phone, or in person.

option-b.value: The FPL Program for Aged & Disabled — 138% FPL, non-MAGI rules
option-b.detail: DHCS's program chart lists "138% FPL = ACA New Adults Ages 19-64; and = FPL Program for Aged & Disabled."

option-b.value: Not subject to the work and community engagement requirements
option-b.detail: "Members who receive Medi-Cal under other coverage groups such as Non-MAGI … are excluded from work and community engagement requirements." A person who moves out of the MAGI New Adult Group stops being assessed for the work rule as of the effective date of the new determination.

option-b.value: Assets are counted: $130,000 for one person through June 30, 2027
option-b.detail: Plus $65,000 per additional household member. From July 1, 2027: $21,000 for one person and $31,000 for two. Countable assets include bank accounts, cash, second vehicles and second homes; your main home, main vehicle and household items are excluded.

option-b.item: Also excluded from the six-month renewal rule
option-b.value: Aged, blind and disabled members keep their annual renewal cycle
option-b.detail: DHCS's briefing lists "Aged, Blind, or Disabled people (including individuals who receive SSI)" among those not subject to the six-month redetermination requirement.

option-b.value: Anyone who has a condition that meets the Social Security Administration's definition of blindness or disability
option-b.detail: The work-rule exclusion for "medically frail or otherwise has special medical needs" expressly includes "an individual who is blind or disabled, as defined in Section 1382c of Title 42." Whether you qualify is a determination for SSA, DHCS, or your county — not something this site can decide.

option-c.value: A private health plan from Covered California with federal premium tax credits and, if you qualify, the California Premium Subsidy
option-c.detail: Covered California is the state marketplace; the federal credit is applied through your tax return.

option-c.value: Household income from 100% to 400% FPL, and not eligible for Medi-Cal
option-c.detail: If you are eligible for Medi-Cal, the marketplace will route you to Medi-Cal instead. "Most consumers up to 138% FPL will be eligible for Medi-Cal."

option-c.value: 0% of income up to 150% FPL; 2.8%–5.28% from 150% to 200% FPL (with the California Premium Subsidy)
option-c.detail: 0% of income up to 150% FPL; 2.8%–5.28% from 150% to 200% FPL (with the California Premium Subsidy). Above 200% FPL the chart shows 6.78%–8.66% (200–250%), 8.66%–10.22% (250–300%) and 10.22% (300–400%), and no state help applies above 200% FPL.
Outside that window you need a qualifying life event.

option-c.item: Why you might not need this
option-c.value: If your MAGI is at or below 138% FPL, Medi-Cal is free and you keep more money
option-c.detail: The work rule is the trade-off: Medi-Cal is cheaper, but from 2027 it comes with the compliance requirement.

option-d.value: Household income above 400% FPL, or after a Medi-Cal work-rule termination
option-d.detail: "400+% FPL = Unsubsidized Coverage" in DHCS's program chart.

option-d.value: Losing Medi-Cal for non-compliance removes your marketplace financial help as well
option-d.detail: "If you lose Medi-Cal because you did not meet these rules, you cannot get financial help to pay for a health plan through Covered California. That means you would have to pay the full cost of new health insurance."

option-d.item: The safety valve in the law
option-d.value: The county must check every other basis of eligibility before denying, and you get a hearing
option-d.detail: WIC § 14005.69(k)(1)(E) and (n). This is why the work-rule consequences are less severe than they first appear: a termination cannot be automatic.

option-d.value: Allowed at any time, with compliance assessed on the new application
option-d.detail: CMS: "Individuals who are disenrolled may reapply at any time and will be assessed for compliance upon reapplication."
